svg.title: One port of a host, its connections from two systems
svg.desc: Three projects. Below, side by side, Product with the host Engine, and Operations with the hosts Console and Agent; Console dials Agent over ConsoleToAgent. Above them, a dashed purple box: Board, a layer that extends both. In Board the host Screen, the connection ScreenToAgent - Screen of one system, Agent of the other, so only Board can declare it - and the multiplexer AgentPort over ScreenToAgent and ConsoleToAgent, an orange box: only Board sees both connections. Agent's port is drawn on Agent; two arrows reach it: from Screen with the first byte Screen.uid, from Console with the first byte Console.uid, and the port hands each socket to its connection. Under each host, where its code is generated from: Engine and Console from their own systems; Screen and Agent from Board - Agent because it listens on the multiplexer Board declares. Footer: a dialing host needs no multiplexer in its project, because every connection carries id, the uid of its own host, the same in every project that sees it; the listening host is generated from the project that declares its multiplexer, so route it only from there.

g.text: One port of a host, its connections from two systems
Board : Product, Operations - the layer that sees both systems
declared in Board: only Board sees both connections
code from Board: it listens on AgentPort
A dialing host needs no multiplexer in its project: every connection carries id - the uid of its own host,
the same in every project that sees it. The listening host comes from the project that declares its multiplexer.
